children: Bank of Japan policymakers likely see room for further interest-rate hikes, supporting market expectations for a December move, according to the minutes of the September meeting. One board member noted that corporate feedback showed past hikes and potential near-term increases had limited impact, with hardly any firms scaling back capital spending over borrowing costs. Another member said recent stock gains and yen weakness had made financial conditions even more accommodative for businesses. With inflation persisting, many economists expect the terminal rate to exceed 1.75%. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
